items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: some cats standing close to the bandstand who knew the personnel of Duke's orchestra started asking very loudly: 'Where is Johnny Hodges? Where is Freddie Jenkins? Where is Barney Bigard?'

ctx.x: He must have had 10 blow outs and the inkertubes had more patches on them than flies in ano open sugar barrel. I thought we'd never make it to Atlantic City on time but we did. The dance was on the pier in a place that was usually reserved for the white public but this night, it was for a Negro dance. The band was under the leadership of Benny Carter but I dont remember who the other members were except Cour//ance and Mack Horton on trombone.

We got on the bandstand and after a couple of numbers, some cats standing close to the bandstand who knew the personnel of Duke's orchestra started asking very loudly: "Where is Johnny Hodges? Where is Freddie Jenkins? Where is Barney Bigard?' and so on... When Fletcher Henderson had a pick up band playing under his name in New Jersey, he did come on the gig and direct the musicians for a while, but Duke was in New York at the Cotton Club and no one in the orchestra resembled Duke. What an embarrassing night.....

I had been in touch by correspondence with Charles Delaunay of the Hot Club de France who told me in a letter that he was trying to arrange something in Paris that would bring me back there. Charles had been in New York shortly after my return from Japan. I had met him and told him of my desire to come back to France. He told me that things were not the same then as before the war, but if I wanted to give it a try, he would see what he could do, but he wouldn't promise anything.
